title: Token-budgeted admission controller with latency-safe truncation and fallback templates
creator: Marcus Li
description:
Problem: Sudden tenant spikes and cost-heavy prompts (long context + compute-heavy post-processing) are causing tail latency breaches and unpredictable token spend for hosted customers. Current admission heuristics are coarse (per-tenant QPS) and cannot account for variable token cost per request or optional post-processing steps (reranking, tool calls, rerenders).

Goal: Implement a token-budgeted admission controller that: 1) predicts request token cost at admission time, 2) enforces a per-tenant token budget and soft quotas, and 3) supports latency-safe degradation strategies including deterministic output truncation, dropping optional post-processing stages, and swapping to compact fallback templates or model variants. The feature must preserve SLOs (p99 latency), keep customer interruption visible (headers/response flags), and be observable for rollout and tuning.
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller computes a token-cost estimate for >=90% of incoming requests within 2ms of arrival
Per-tenant token budgets enforced at runtime with configurable windows (minute/10m) and burst allowances
When budget would be exceeded, controller chooses a degradation action (truncate, drop rerank, fallback template, or soft-reject) according to policy and applies it deterministically
Telemetry emitted for admission decision, estimated vs actual token cost, chosen degradation action, and latency impact
Canary rollout completes to 5% of serving traffic without SLO regressions; automated rollback triggers on p99 latency > 120% of baseline
Documentation and runbook updated with diagnostics and mitigation steps
runbook: If canary p99 latency increases >20%: abort rollout, revert PRs, and notify SRE on call
To debug decision for a request: use request-id -> admission logs -> estimator compare table
If budget starvation observed for high-paying tenants: escalate to billing + PM for quota adjustments
updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff design doc complete; scoped estimator model (linear predictor based on prompt length, prompt type, and feature flags).

2026-03-11: Benchmarked estimator against 50k sampled requests from last 7 days: median estimation error 12%, 95th percentile 28%. Meeting scheduled with runtime team to optimize microbenchmark kernel accounting.

2026-03-12: Prototype PR opened (see PR link). Initial admission hook injected into front-door request pipeline; chosen default degradation order: 1) deterministic truncation, 2) drop rerank, 3) compact template fallback, 4) soft-reject with Retry-After. UX flagged for PM review so customers receive clear headers when degraded.

2026-03-12: Design review feedback from Alice Moreno (PM) and Ben Kaur (SRE): request to add per-region policy overrides for multi-region failover scenarios and to ensure estimator operates on the pre-tokenized prompt to avoid compute overhead. Added to next steps.

2026-03-12: Added synthetic load test to CI that simulates 3x traffic spike with skewed heavy-token requests; prototype preserved p95 but p99 regressed by 15% under current config. Next action: introduce burst credit bank and tune degradation thresholds.
implementation_notes: Admission hook is implemented as a non-blocking filter in the front-door service to keep latency impact minimal
Estimator runs on a compact feature vector; we will ship the linear fallback and later iterate to an ML model if error warrants it
Degradation actions must be idempotent and signalled via response headers: X-RW-Degraded:true; X-RW-Degradation-Reason:truncation
Fallback templates stored in config service and can be edited by PMs; ensure template size limits to avoid token surprises
risks: Estimator under-prediction could allow expensive requests through and break SLOs; mitigated by conservative safety factor and circuit-breaker on observed variance
Overly aggressive truncation could materially degrade customer experience for small subset of customers — add AB test for UX acceptability
Interplay with multi-region failover: budgets must be coordinated or region-local budgets applied to avoid double-counting or silent rejection during failover
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Canary to 1% of traffic (non-tenant-critical) with verbose telemetry
Stage 2: Canary to 5% and run 48h SLO comparison; if stable, proceed
Stage 3: Gradual ramp to 25% with per-tenant opt-out flag for strategic customers
Stage 4: Full rollout and deprecation of legacy coarse admission heuristics
